subject: reading
title: Kate and the Wren
about: A wren gets stuck in the kitchen, and Kate catches it in a cage only to set it free in the garden. The story practises the Unit 5 spellings tch (kitchen, latched, unlatched), soft g and ge (large, cage), ve (five, live, have) and wr (wren, wrapped), plus past-tense -ed read as /t/ (flapped, bumped, hopped) and as /d/ (grinned, waved), with the tricky word how. It is decodable at CKLA Unit 5, which the class usually reaches in March.
tip: Have him read the -ed words aloud and listen: flapped ends in /t/, waved ends in /d/, and lifted adds a whole extra syllable.

passage.text:
On Tuesday a wren flapped in from the porch.
It was stuck in the kitchen.
It bumped the lamp.
"How did a wren get in?" said Kate.

Kate got a large cage.
She set five seeds in it.
The wren hopped in.
Kate latched the cage.
She wrapped a cloth on the cage.
The wren sat still.

***
Kate lifted the cage.
She took it to the garden.
She unlatched the cage.
The wren flapped up to a branch.
It sang and sang.

Kate grinned and waved.
"Have fun, little wren!" she said.
"You can live in the garden."

cards.note: Kate gets the cage to catch the wren.
The wren flapped in from the porch and got stuck in the kitchen.

cards.q: What did Kate set in the cage?
cards.note: Five seeds tempt the wren to hop in.

cards.q: What did Kate wrap on the cage?
cards.note: A cloth over the cage helps a bird sit still.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The wren flapping in from the porch is the very first thing that happens.

cards.q: At the end, where does the wren go?
cards.note: Kate unlatches the cage and the wren flaps up to a branch.

cards.q: How did Kate feel when the wren sang?
cards.note: Grinning and waving show that Kate is glad.

cards.q: Why did Kate take the cage to the garden?
cards.note: Kate catches the wren only to carry it outside and let it go.

cards.q: What does latched mean in the story?
cards.note: To latch a cage is to shut its little lock so the door stays closed.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: All three start with the silent w of wr; only wren is in the story.
